1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 c6 3.g3.strategy: Prepares the king's fianchetto, the set-up that gives the opening its character: the bishop will bear on the centre from the long diagonal instead of White occupying it with pawns. White keeps a central pawn advance and a queenside fianchetto in reserve and plays a patient, flexible game.

1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 c6 3.b3.strategy: Prepares the queen's bishop on the long diagonal, aiming at e5 and the black kingside, and leaves open how the king's bishop will develop. White still controls the centre with pieces rather than pawns, but has to be patient against Black's solid c6 and d5 pawns.
1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 c6 3.b3.name: Réti Opening: Anglo-Slav Variation, Bogoljubow Variation

1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 c6 3.e3.strategy: A solid, flexible choice: the pawn frees the king's bishop and keeps a classical pawn centre available if Black allows it. The price is that it closes the queen's bishop's own diagonal, and White gives up the kingside fianchetto that gives this opening its character.
1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 c6 3.e3.name: Réti Opening: Anglo-Slav Variation, Gurevich System

1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 c6 3.e3 Nf6.strategy: The natural developing move: the knight adds a defender to d5 and takes the e4 square from White, so White cannot easily build a centre with the e-pawn. Black stays flexible about where to place the queen's bishop and how to complete the pawn chain.

1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 c6 3.g3 Nf6.strategy: Develops the knight, puts a second defender on d5 and takes control of e4. Black gets a harmonious development: the knight and the c6 and d5 pawns hold the centre while the c8-bishop is still free to choose its post.

1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 c6 3.b3 Bf5.name: Réti Opening: Anglo-Slav Variation, Bogoljubow Variation
1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 c6 3.b3 Bf5.strategy: Develops the bishop outside the chain before ...e6 shuts it in, solving the c8-bishop's problem early, and keeps the queen from coming to c2. Black continues with a solid centre while White still has to decide where the king's bishop goes.

1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 c6 3.b3 Bg4.strategy: Develops the bishop outside the chain with an eye on the f3 knight, which holds the e5 and d4 squares. A trade on f3 forces White to recapture with a pawn and double White's pawns.
1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 c6 3.b3 Bg4.name: Réti Opening: Anglo-Slav Variation, Bogoljubow Variation

1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 c6 3.b3 Bf5 4.Bb2.name: Réti Opening: Anglo-Slav Variation, Bogoljubow Variation
1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 c6 3.b3 Bf5 4.Bb2.strategy: Brings the queen's bishop to the long diagonal at once, where it aims at e5 and, behind it, the black kingside. White has fianchettoed first and keeps the choice for the king's bishop open; the pieces rather than pawns pressure the centre.

1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 c6 3.e3 Nf6 4.Nc3.strategy: Brings the last minor piece out to its natural square, where it joins the c4 pawn in the pressure on d5 and supports a later central pawn break. White decides for classical development with pieces in the centre, and a queenside fianchetto remains possible.

1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 c6 3.e3 Nf6 4.Qc2.name: Réti Opening: Anglo-Slav Variation, Gurevich System
1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 c6 3.e3 Nf6 4.Qc2.strategy: Guards the c4 pawn and stops ...Bf5, which would simply hang to the queen. The queen also stands behind a later central advance, but the queen's knight and bishop are still at home, so Black gets time to finish a compact development.

1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 c6 3.e3 Nf6 4.Nc3 e6.strategy: Builds the solid chain c6, d5 and e6, so d5 is guarded for good and the king's bishop is free to develop. The price is the queen's bishop, which is shut in behind its own pawns; Black accepts a slightly passive but sound structure for it.

1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 c6 3.e3 Nf6 4.Nc3 Nbd7.strategy: Develops the knight to a square from which it supports a later ...e5 central break. The cost is that the knight blocks the c8-bishop's diagonal, so the bishop has to find a route another way before Black is fully developed.

1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 c6 3.e3 Nf6 4.Nc3 e6 5.b3.strategy: Keeps the opening's spirit: instead of a central pawn advance, White prepares the queen's bishop on the long diagonal and defends the c4 pawn with a pawn. The position stays flexible and White controls the centre with pieces, at the cost of having no central space yet.

1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 c6 3.e3 Nf6 4.Nc3 e6 5.b3.name: Réti Opening: Anglo-Slav Variation, Gurevich System
1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 c6 3.e3 Nf6 4.Nc3 e6 5.b3.strategy: Puts the bishop on an active diagonal, controlling the e5 square and pointing at the h2 pawn, and prepares castling. Black builds a compact set-up in which the bishop supports a later ...e5 break.

Completes the queen's fianchetto: the bishop looks at e5 and the long diagonal, though the knight on c3 blocks it for now. White has chosen piece play over a central pawn advance, and Black's bishop on d6 stands ready to answer on e5.

Gets the king to safety before the centre opens and connects the rooks. Black's chain on c6, d5 and e6 with the bishop on d6 is compact and sound; its one remaining problem is the c8-bishop, which still has to be freed.

1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 c6 3.e3 Nf6 4.Nc3 Nbd7 5.b.strategy: Defends c4 with a pawn and prepares the queen's bishop on the long diagonal. White answers the knight on d7 with a flexible fianchetto development rather than a central advance, and the knight on c3 is free to move without costing the c4 pawn.

1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 c6 3.e3 Nf6 4.Nc3 Nbd7 5.Q.name: Réti Opening: Anglo-Slav Variation, Gurevich System
1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 c6 3.e3 Nf6 4.Nc3 Nbd7 5.Q.strategy: Guards the c4 pawn so that ...dxc4 can be answered by an immediate recapture, and places the queen behind a possible central advance. White keeps a classical set-up, but the queen's bishop stays shut in behind the e3 pawn and needs a plan of its own.

1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 c6 3.e3 Nf6 4.Nc3 Nbd7 5.b.name: Réti Opening: Anglo-Slav Variation, Gurevich System
1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 c6 3.e3 Nf6 4.Nc3 Nbd7 5.b.strategy: Black claims the centre with the e-pawn. It is defended by the knight on d7, so taking it only loses a knight for a pawn. The price is that the pawns on d5 and e5 become targets, and the c8-bishop is still shut in behind the d7 knight.

1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 c6 3.g3 Nf6 4.Bg2.name: Réti Opening: Anglo-Slav Variation, with g3
1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 c6 3.g3 Nf6 4.Bg2.strategy: Completes the king's fianchetto: the bishop stands behind the f3 knight on the long diagonal, supports the centre from a distance and clears the way for castling. White commits to a patient, flexible game in which pieces rather than pawns press on Black's centre.

1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 c6 3.g3 Nf6 4.b3.name: Réti Opening: Anglo-Slav Variation
1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 c6 3.g3 Nf6 4.b3.strategy: Prepares the queen's bishop first and guards the c4 pawn with a pawn, which lets White put off the king's bishop. The price is that castling is delayed, and Black has time to bring out the light-squared bishop first.

1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 c6 3.g3 Nf6 4.b3 Bf5.name: Réti Opening: Anglo-Slav Variation, London Defensive System
1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 c6 3.g3 Nf6 4.b3 Bf5.strategy: Develops the light-squared bishop outside the pawn chain before ...e6 can lock it in, the usual way to deal with the problem piece of this structure. It also keeps the queen from c2, where the bishop would take it.

1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 c6 3.g3 Nf6 4.b3 Bg4.name: Réti Opening: Anglo-Slav Variation, Torre System
1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 c6 3.g3 Nf6 4.b3 Bg4.strategy: Develops the bishop outside the chain with pressure on the f3 knight, which holds e5 and d4. Trading it for the knight takes away a defender of those squares, though White then has the bishop pair; White can also ask the bishop a question at once with h3.

1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 c6 3.g3 Nf6 4.b3 g6.name: Réti Opening: Anglo-Slav Variation, with g3
1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 c6 3.g3 Nf6 4.b3 g6.strategy: Mirrors White's plan with a fianchetto of Black's own: the bishop on g7 will contest the long diagonal, and the c6 and d5 pawns keep the centre solid. The game becomes a slow manoeuvring fight in which neither side quickly takes space in the centre.

1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 c6 3.g3 Nf6 4.b3 dxc4.name: Réti Opening: Anglo-Slav Variation, with dxc4
1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 c6 3.g3 Nf6 4.b3 dxc4.strategy: Gives up the d5 pawn's central presence. White recaptures with the b-pawn and gets an open b-file and a clear long diagonal for the queen's bishop. Playable, but White's pieces gain scope.

1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 c6 3.g3 Nf6 4.Bg2 e6.strategy: Builds the solid chain c6, d5 and e6, which makes d5 safe against the pressure of White's pieces and frees the king's bishop. The price is the c8-bishop, which is shut in behind the chain, so Black accepts a slow, strategic game.

1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 c6 3.g3 Nf6 4.Bg2 dxc4.name: Réti Opening: Anglo-Slav Variation, with g3
1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 c6 3.g3 Nf6 4.Bg2 dxc4.strategy: Grabs the pawn and releases the tension in the centre. White can usually win it back while developing, so Black should treat it as a loan and aim for a safe structure rather than cling to it.

1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 c6 3.g3 Nf6 4.Bg2 Bf5.name: Réti Opening: Anglo-Slav Variation, with g3
1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 c6 3.g3 Nf6 4.Bg2 Bf5.strategy: Develops the light-squared bishop outside the pawn chain before ...e6 can lock it in. With the f3 knight still blocking White's bishop, Black can complete development quietly and then close the centre on its own terms.

1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 c6 3.g3 Nf6 4.b3 Bf5 5.Bg2.name: Réti Opening: Anglo-Slav Variation, London Defensive System
1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 c6 3.g3 Nf6 4.b3 Bf5 5.Bg2.strategy: Completes the kingside fianchetto and clears the way to castling; the queen's bishop follows to the long diagonal next. White controls the centre from a distance with pieces, as the opening intends, while Black's f5 bishop is already developed outside the chain.

1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 c6 3.g3 Nf6 4.b3 Bf5 5.Bb2.name: Réti Opening: Anglo-Slav Variation, London Defensive System
1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 c6 3.g3 Nf6 4.b3 Bf5 5.Bb2.strategy: Brings the queen's bishop to the long diagonal at once, aiming at e5 and the black kingside, and delays the king's bishop. It is the other order of the same fianchetto set-up, at the cost of keeping the king in the centre a move longer.

1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 c6 3.g3 Nf6 4.b3 Bf5 5.Bg2.strategy: Black gets a complete, solid set-up before White's second bishop arrives: d5 is safe, the f8-bishop is free to develop, and the bishop on f5 stays outside the pawn chain.

1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 c6 3.g3 Nf6 4.b3 Bf5 5.Bg2.name: Réti Opening: Anglo-Slav Variation, London Defensive System
1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 c6 3.g3 Nf6 4.b3 Bf5 5.Bg2.strategy: Completes the double fianchetto: both bishops watch the long diagonals and the b3 pawn guards c4, while White is ready to castle. White controls the centre from a distance with pieces, and Black has to prove that c6, d5 and e6 hold.

1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 c6 3.g3 Nf6 4.b3 Bg4 5.Bg2.name: Réti Opening: Anglo-Slav Variation, Torre System
1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 c6 3.g3 Nf6 4.b3 Bg4 5.Bg2.strategy: Develops the king's bishop and prepares castling, ignoring the bishop on g4: if it takes on f3, the bishop recaptures and then eyes d5 from there. White keeps a flexible, fianchettoed position.

1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 c6 3.g3 Nf6 4.b3 Bg4 5.Bb2.name: Réti Opening: Anglo-Slav Variation, Torre System
1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 c6 3.g3 Nf6 4.b3 Bg4 5.Bb2.strategy: Develops the queen's bishop first, but the king's bishop is still at home: ...Bxf3 forces White to recapture with the e-pawn, which doubles White's pawns. White keeps both bishops in return, a structural concession that Bg2 first avoids.

1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 c6 3.g3 Nf6 4.b3 Bg4 5.Bg2.strategy: Supports the d5 pawn and frees the f8-bishop, keeping the bishop on g4 outside the chain and pressing on the f3 knight. Black has a complete, solid structure with a bishop that is already developed.

1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 c6 3.g3 Nf6 4.b3 Bg4 5.Bg2.name: Réti Opening: Anglo-Slav Variation, Torre System
1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 c6 3.g3 Nf6 4.b3 Bg4 5.Bg2.strategy: Completes the double fianchetto: the bishops on b2 and g2 aim along both long diagonals and the b3 pawn guards c4. The f3 knight is under pressure from the g4 bishop but is defended by the bishop and the e2 pawn.

1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 c6 3.g3 Nf6 4.Bg2 Bf5 5.O-.strategy: Castles behind the bishop and the g3 pawn, a robust shelter that leaves White free to play in the centre and on the queenside. There is no hurry to open the position: the fianchetto structure is solid and the king is out of the centre.

Supports the d5 pawn once more and opens the f8-bishop, while the bishop on f5 stays outside the chain. Black has a complete, solid set-up with d5 well defended, and the structure gives White little to attack at once.

1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 c6 3.g3 Nf6 4.Bg2 Bf5 5.O-.name: Réti Opening: Anglo-Slav Variation, with g3
1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 c6 3.g3 Nf6 4.Bg2 Bf5 5.O-.strategy: Blocks the f5 bishop's diagonal towards b1 and c2 and prepares a central advance with the e-pawn to challenge it. White accepts a modest, flexible set-up that stays closed and manoeuvring.
